title: PhysGuard: Fisher-Guided Gradient Projection for Sim-to-Real Neural PDE Surrogates
claim: A baseline model loses core low-frequency structure after transfer; our adaptation preserves it, as the fields and spectra show.
layout: 2 columns, top fields over bottom spectra, red-vs-green contrast, annotated arrows
description: A 2x2 grid compares a pretrained baseline (left, red title, grey border) with the proposed method (right, green title, green border). The top row has two heatmaps of a fluid velocity field, in red-blue diverging colors with white streamlines. The baseline field is blurry and weak. The PhysGuard field has sharp, strong vortex structures. Blue upward arrows link each field to its spectrum below. The bottom row has log-log plots of 2D FFT power spectrum against wavenumber. Each plot compares a dashed ground-truth curve with a solid model curve. Shaded blue marks the low-frequency region and tan marks the high-frequency region. On the left, a red filled gap with the red label 'Core physical loss' shows the shortfall. On the right, a smaller green gap with the green label 'Low-frequency preserved' shows the fix. The eye goes first to the red and green titles and the annotations.
caption: Predicted fields (top) and power spectra (bottom) for the simulation-pretrained model (left) and the same model after PhysGuard fine-tuning on real data (right). Dashed curves show the ground truth. PhysGuard better matches the ground-truth spectrum at low frequencies. Best viewed in color.
abstract: Neural operator models trained on simulation data often lose accuracy when applied to experimental measurements due to the sim-to-real gap. Standard fine-tuning with limited real data can reduce this gap, but it may also damage the core physics-relevant representations learned during pretraining. Although knowledge-preserving adaptation has been widely investigated in vision or language tasks, it remains unclear whether these methods are suitable for neural operators whose architectures and protected knowledge are fundamentally different. Neural operators need to preserve core-scale physical structures rather than semantic or visual features. We propose PhysGuard, a physics-preserving framework for accurate sim-to-real adaptation of neural operators. Specifically, PhysGuard uses the empirical Fisher Information Matrix computed on simulation data to identify physics-critical parameter directions, then restricts fine-tuning updates to directions that do not interfere with them. A layer-wise Gram-matrix formulation makes this efficient for models with millions of parameters, while an adaptive threshold automatically determines the protected subspace size. A spectral probe experiment shows that the dominant Fisher directions are strongly associated with low-frequency output structures. Experiments on benchmark across four neural operator architectures and different physical systems show that PhysGuard performs strongly on most evaluation metrics compared to baselines. The benefits are most evident under severe domain shift, where it reduces low-frequency error by up to 32% compared to standard fine-tuning while maintaining adaptability. Our code is available at https://github.com/Data-Driven-Computational-Geotechnics/PhysGuard.
